extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients, PD/PIs, and institutional grant administrators preparing/submitting RPPRs
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting NIH Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) — annual, interim, and final — including what content to include, which RPPR type to file, and how/when to submit via eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to describe a grant’s scientific progress, identify significant changes, report on personnel, and describe plans for the subsequent budget period or year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an annual report that summarizes scientific progress, documents any significant changes to the project, reports on personnel (senior/key persons and other relevant staff), and outlines plans for the next budget period or year. Submit annually using the RPPR mechanism in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when submitting a renewal (Type 2) application. If the Type 2 is not funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the Final RPPR for the project. If the Type 2 is funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the annual RPPR for the final year of the previous competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Interim RPPR when a renewal (Type 2) application is submitted. Note the conditional outcomes: if the renewal is not awarded, the Interim RPPR becomes the Final RPPR; if funded, it becomes the annual RPPR for the final year of the prior competitive segment. The data elements collected on the Interim RPPR are the same as for the Final RPPR, including project outcomes — ensure those elements are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use as part of the grant closeout process to submit project outcomes in addition to the information submitted on the annual RPPR. A final progress report is required for any grant that has passed its project end date and will not be extended through award of a new competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a grant has reached its project end date and will not be continued by a new competitive segment, submit a Final RPPR through the closeout module. The Final RPPR must include project outcomes as well as the standard annual RPPR information. This is a required closeout deliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and timing (access via eRA Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no RPPR form available for download. Submit RPPR data through the eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access each RPPR type via the Commons Status tab in eRA Commons — there is no standalone downloadable form. The Interim RPPR link appears one day after the project segment end date (but before closeout). The Final RPPR link becomes available through the closeout module once the grant is eligible for closeout. Follow these timing rules to select and submit the correct RPPR type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH RPPR Instruction Guide and Help resources
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH RPPR Instruction Guide (PDF) and NIH RPPR Online Help are provided as the official instructions for completing RPPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NIH RPPR Instruction Guide (PDF), the NIH RPPR Online Help, RPPR Help & Tutorials, and related documents such as 'RPPRs: Who Can Do What?' and the Final Invention Statement for detailed instructions, definitions of data elements, role-based permissions, examples, and procedural details. These resources provide the authoritative completion and submission guidance.
